mainTopic: Feeding a sick person on יום כיפור (patient versus doctor), and the new משנה on life-saving cases: בולמוס, the mad dog, throat pain, the collapse, and which forbidden food to feed first.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story: the child of the pregnant woman who could not overcome her craving on יום כיפור grew up to be the wicked שבתאי, the fruit-hoarder. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a חולה is fed על פי בקיאין, on the advice of experts. רבי ינאי rules that if the patient says he needs food we listen to him, because לב יודע מרת נפשו. If the doctor says he needs food, we listen to the doctor, because the illness has confused the patient. The גמרא tests these rules against the exact wording of the משנה. It concludes that in ספק נפשות, two experts who say he needs food are enough, even against a majority. מר בר רב אשי goes further: a patient who says 'I need' is fed even if a hundred experts disagree. A new משנה then lists more life-saving cases: feeding forbidden food to a person with בולמוס, the disputed mad-dog remedy, medicine for throat pain on שבת, and digging out someone buried under a collapse. The גמרא explains the sign that the person with בולמוס has recovered, and rules that he is fed the lightest prohibition first. It ends with the dispute over whether to feed him טבל or תרומה when the טבל cannot be tithed.

steps.title: The end of the story: the wicked child שבתאי
steps.stepSummary: The previous story ends. The woman's craving could not be calmed, and the child born from her was שבתאי, who hoarded fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wicked are estranged from the womb. Shabbetai, the hoarder of fruits, came out of her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story on the previous amud. A pregnant woman craved food on יום כיפור, and whispering to her did not calm her, so רבי חנינא applied a פסוק to her. Her child turned out to be the wicked שבתאי אוצר פירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק זורו רשעים מרחם teaches that a wicked nature can show itself even before birth. The proof was the child's later behavior: שבתאי hoarded produce in famine years to raise prices and profit from the poor. The story is now closed, and the גמרא will move on to a new line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked are estranged from the womb (תהלים נח:ד)
Came out of her (was born from her)
Hoarder of fruits, someone who stockpiled produce to inflate prices

steps.confusionAlert: Here נפק מינה means literally that someone came out of her, that is, was born from her. It is not the common technical phrase נפקא מינה, meaning a practical difference.

phrases.english: The wicked are estranged from the womb.
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from תהלים נח:ד, and here it's applied to the unborn child in the story.

phrases.english: Shabbetai the hoarder of fruits came out of her.
phrases.notes: He hoarded produce during famines to profit at the expense of the poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story about the pregnant woman that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The child whose craving could not be calmed grew up to be the wicked שבתאי, which fulfilled the פסוק זורו רשעים מרחם.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: feed a sick person on the advice of experts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a חולה who needs food on יום כיפור is fed על פי בקיאין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sick person: we feed him according to the experts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares for רבי ינאי's rulings in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a sick person may eat on יום כיפור if experts say he needs to. It does not say what to do when the sick person and the doctor disagree. That gap is exactly what רבי ינאי will address.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person
We feed him
According to experts (people with medical knowledge)

phrases.english: A sick person: we feed him
according to experts.
phrases.notes: The plural wording, experts, becomes important here.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹלֶה מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פִּי בְּקִיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story behind and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick person is fed on יום כיפור according to the judgment of experts.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: when the patient says he needs food, we listen to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי rules that if the חולה says he needs to eat and the רופא says he does not, we listen to the חולה. His source is the פסוק לב יודע מרת נפשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: If a sick person says he needs to eat and a doctor says he does not, we listen to the sick person. What is the reason? The verse says, The heart knows the bitterness of its own soul.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי gives a rule for a disagreement between the sick person and the doctor. In this case the sick person wins, and a פסוק is brought as the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the patient can truly feel how weak or in pain he is. So when he says he needs food, we feed him even against the doctor's opinion. The פסוק from משלי teaches that a person's own heart knows his inner suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: A doctor
He needs (to eat)
We listen to the sick person
What is the reason?
The heart knows the bitterness of its soul (משלי יד:י)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a basic rule in הלכה: a sick person's own sense that he needs food can override a doctor's opinion when פיקוח נפש may be at stake.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
If the sick person says he needs to eat,
and the doctor says he does not need to,
we listen to the sick person.
What is the reason?
The heart knows the bitterness of its own soul.
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from משלי יד:י.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: חוֹלֶה אוֹמֵר צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule for a case the משנה left open: a disagreement between the patient and the doctor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the חולה says he needs food and the רופא disagrees, we follow the חולה, because לב יודע מרת נפשו.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ינאי needed to say this, since it seems obvious that a person knows his own body best.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ינאי bothered to state such an obvious rule. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the heart really knows its own pain, then of course we should listen to the patient. A rule that seems self-evident needs a reason for being stated, so the גמרא looks for the mistake someone might otherwise have made.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (Why say it?)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבי ינאי's first ruling needed to be said at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's ruling that we listen to the חולה who says he needs food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems too obvious to need saying, since everyone knows a person feels his own suffering best.

steps.title: Without this ruling we would think the doctor knows better
steps.stepSummary: The answer: without the ruling, we might have assumed the רופא's expertise outweighs the patient's feelings. רבי ינאי teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the doctor is more certain, since he is the expert. So it teaches us that we still listen to the sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of the previous step. It explains the mistake we might have made if רבי ינאי had not spoken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken assumption (the מהו דתימא) was that a trained doctor has more reliable knowledge than a patient's own feelings. רבי ינאי's ruling corrects this: when it comes to needing food, the patient's inner sense outweighs the doctor's expertise.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
He knows more surely, he is more certain
It teaches us (this is the new point)

phrases.english: You might have said:
the doctor knows it more surely,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רוֹפֵא קִים לֵיהּ טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: identifying the mistaken assumption the ruling comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A doctor's professional knowledge is more reliable than the patient's own feeling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The patient's own sense that he needs food overrides the doctor's opinion.

steps.title: The reverse case: when the doctor says he needs food, we listen to the doctor
steps.stepSummary: If the רופא says the patient needs food and the חולה says he does not, we listen to the רופא, because the patient's illness has confused him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a doctor says he needs to eat and the sick person says he does not, we listen to the doctor. What is the reason? Confusion has taken hold of the sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי ינאי's teaching with the opposite case. This time the doctor wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This might look like a contradiction of the previous ruling, but it is not. When the patient says he does not need food, we suspect the illness has dulled his judgment (תונבא). In both cases the result leans toward feeding him and protecting his life.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not need (to eat)
Confusion or mental fog caused by illness
That has taken hold of him

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a contradiction. The rule is not that either the patient or the doctor is always trusted. Whoever says the patient needs to eat is the one we follow.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ינאי, if either the חולה or the רופא says food is needed, we feed him. The patient's own feeling outweighs the doctor (לב יודע מרת נפשו), and a confused patient's refusal does not outweigh the doctor (תונבא).

phrases.english: If the doctor says he needs to eat,
and the sick person says he does not need to,
we listen to the doctor.
What is the reason?
It is confusion that has taken hold of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רוֹפֵא אוֹמֵר צָרִיךְ, וְחוֹלֶה אוֹמֵר אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image case of רבי ינאי's first ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the רופא says food is needed and the חולה refuses, we follow the רופא, because the illness has confused the patient.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: experts count, not the patient himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's words על פי בקיאין that we feed the patient only on the experts' word, not on his own. This seems to contradict רבי ינאי's first ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: A sick person is fed according to experts. According to experts, yes; according to himself, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי by reading the משנה's wording closely (a דיוק). It suggests that the patient's own word is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only experts, which seems to imply that the patient's own claim does not count. But רבי ינאי said we listen to a patient who says he needs to eat, even against the doctor. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No
According to himself (by his own word)

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah: a sick person
is fed according to experts.
According to experts, yes;
according to himself, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: חוֹלֶה — מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פִּי בְּקִיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the משנה to test רבי ינאי's rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's ruling that we listen to the חולה who says he needs food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only experts, which implies the patient's own word cannot be relied on. That conflicts with trusting the patient over the doctor.

steps.title: Second inference: several experts, not just one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a second inference from the plural בקיאין: we need several experts, not one. This seems to contradict רבי ינאי's ruling that one רופא overrides the patient.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to experts, yes; according to one expert, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second precise reading of the same משנה. This time the focus is the plural word for experts, and it adds another difficulty for רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural בקיאין suggests that at least two experts are needed. But רבי ינאי ruled that a single רופא saying the patient needs food overrides the patient's refusal. Step 9 first answers the challenge of Step 7, and Steps 10 and 11 then resolve this one.

keyTerms.meaning: A single expert
Plural wording (the source of this inference)
A precise inference from the exact wording of a text

steps.confusionAlert: Rows 1 and 2 of this step have the same pattern as the previous step, but the target is different. Step 7 contrasted experts with the patient himself. This step contrasts several experts with one expert.

phrases.english: According to experts, yes;
according to one expert, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל פִּי בְּקִיאִין — אִין, עַל פִּי בָּקִי אֶחָד — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second inference from the same משנה, aimed at a different part of רבי ינאי's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's ruling that a single רופא overrides the חולה who refuses food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural בקיאין implies that one expert is not enough, yet רבי ינאי relies on one doctor.

steps.title: The משנה is about a patient who says he does not need food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the first challenge. The משנה is talking about a patient who says he does not need to eat, so the experts decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the patient says: I do not need to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. It explains that the משנה is talking about a patient who says he does NOT need food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 it looked like the משנה ignores the patient's own claim that he needs food, which would contradict רבי ינאי. The answer is that the משנה is not about that case at all. It is about a patient who says he is fine, and in that case we feed him because the experts say so, not because of what he says.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This is a standard way of narrowing a source to a specific case.
I do not need (food)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he says: I do not need (to eat).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first inference (Step 7) by limiting the משנה to a patient who says he does not need food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to ignore a patient who says he needs food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a patient who says he does not need food, so the experts decide. This fits רבי ינאי.

steps.title: Why not feed him based on just one expert?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the second challenge. Even if the patient says he does not need food, רבי ינאי said one רופא is enough. So why does the משנה say experts in the plural?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let them feed him based on one expert!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Even in the case of a patient who says he does not need food, רבי ינאי said one רופא is enough, so why does the משנה need several experts?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 answered the first challenge but not the second one from Step 8. רבי ינאי ruled that one רופא overrides the patient. The plural בקיאין still seems to contradict that.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them feed him
One expert (singular)

phrases.english: But let them feed him
according to one expert!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the second challenge (Step 8) within the case set up in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plural word בקיאין in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ינאי said one רופא is enough against a patient who says he is fine. So why would the משנה require more than one?

steps.title: Plural experts are needed when another expert disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The plural is needed when a second expert says the patient does not need food. In that case we feed him based on experts, meaning two.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the plural is needed when there is another expert with him who says the patient does not need food. Then we feed him based on experts, meaning two who say he needs it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the experts disagree. Another expert says he does not need food, so we feed him only if two experts say he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי's rule of one רופא applies when no other expert disagrees. Once another expert says the patient does not need food, the משנה requires two experts who say he does. So the plural בקיאין fits this new case and does not contradict רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed for this case. This introduces the specific situation where a ruling is necessary.
Another (expert) along with him

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where there is another (expert) with him
who says: he does not need (to eat)
we feed him according to experts (two who say he needs).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by placing the plural in a case where the experts disagree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural בקיאין seemed to contradict רבי ינאי's rule of one רופא.
steps.terutzMaskana: One רופא is enough when no one disagrees. When another expert disagrees, two experts saying he needs food are needed.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious, since we are lenient when a life may be at risk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: two experts against one is clearly enough, since in ספק נפשות we always lean toward feeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! It is a case of doubt about a life, and when a life may be at risk we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה would need to teach the case from Step 11. It seems obvious that we feed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is any doubt that a life is in danger, we break יום כיפור. If two experts say he needs food and only one disagrees, there is clearly a doubt, so of course we feed him. That makes the משנה's teaching seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. This challenges a teaching as unnecessary.
A doubt about whether a life is in danger
To be lenient (here, to let him eat)

phrases.english: It is obvious!
It is a case of doubt about a life,
and in a doubt about a life we are lenient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 11 as teaching something obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case from Step 11 (two experts against one)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule of ספק נפשות להקל already tells us to feed him, so the משנה would not need to teach it.

steps.title: The case is two experts against two experts plus the patient
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where two other experts, along with the patient, say he does not need food.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where there are two other experts, together with the patient, who say he does not need food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the case harder. It is two experts saying he needs food against two experts plus the patient saying he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the side saying he does not need food has more voices: three against two. Here the ruling is no longer obvious. The next step explains why we might have thought we should not feed him.

keyTerms.meaning: Two other (experts)
Who say (plural)

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where there are two other (experts) with him (the patient)
who say: he does not need (to eat).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִיכָּא תְּרֵי אַחֲרִינֵי בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by moving to a harder case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two against one is obviously enough to feed him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches the harder case: two experts against two experts plus the patient.

steps.title: Why we might have followed the majority of opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא taught that two witnesses equal a hundred, but that applies only to testimony. When estimating a situation we follow the majority of opinions, so we might have thought the three voices win.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though רב ספרא said that two witnesses are like a hundred and a hundred are like two, that is only for testimony. When estimating a situation, we follow the majority of opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the case in Step 13 is not obvious. We might have thought the larger group should win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עדות, two witnesses are a complete set, so more witnesses add nothing. A medical judgment is not עדות, though. It is an estimate (אומדנא), and for estimates we count opinions. Two experts plus the patient are a majority, so we might have thought not to feed him.

keyTerms.meaning: Two are like a hundred, and a hundred are like two (for witnesses)
Testimony
An estimate or assessment of a situation
We follow the majority of opinions

steps.confusionAlert: This step is NOT the final ruling. It only explains the 'we might have thought' (הוה אמינא). The next step shows that in ספק נפשות we feed him anyway.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא:
phrases.english: And even though רב ספרא said:
Two are like one hundred, and one hundred are like two,
that applies to matters of testimony,
but in matters of assessment,
we follow the (majority of) opinions.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason we might have ruled differently in the case of Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In an estimate we follow the majority, so two experts plus the patient should beat two experts.
steps.terutzMaskana: This is set up to be rejected in the next step.

steps.title: Following the majority applies only to money, not when a life may be at risk
steps.stepSummary: Following the majority of opinions applies to estimates about money. Here a life may be at risk, so we feed him even against the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that rule applies to estimates about money. Here it is a doubt about a life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer. The rule of majority opinion does not apply when a life may be in danger, so we feed the patient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting opinions works for money cases. When a life may be at stake, two qualified experts saying he needs food create a real ספק נפשות. That is enough to feed him even if more people disagree. This is the new teaching of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An estimate in a money matter
This applies only to... (limits a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: When a life may be in danger, two experts who say the patient needs food are enough. We feed him even if two other experts and the patient himself disagree. Majority opinion decides only in money matters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ספק נפשות is stronger than the normal rule of following the majority. Even a minority opinion of qualified experts is enough to break יום כיפור.

phrases.english: But this applies to assessments about money,
but here it is a doubt about a life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הוה אמינא of Step 14 and gives the final ruling for the case of Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In ספק נפשות, two experts saying the patient needs food outweigh two experts plus the patient. We feed him.

steps.title: The latter clause implies the first clause is about a patient who says he needs food
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that with no experts present we follow the patient. This implies the רישא is about a patient who says he needs food, which goes against Step 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part of the משנה teaches that if there are no experts we feed him based on his own word, it must mean the first part is about a patient who says he needs food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 9. It uses the wording of the second half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says that with no experts we feed him 'on his own word', so he must be saying he needs food. That suggests the רישא is the same patient, only now with experts present. That means the experts decide even against a patient who says he needs food, which goes against רבי ינאי and against Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part (clause) of the משנה
The first part (clause) of the משנה
By implication; it follows that
Based on his own word

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
And if there are no experts there,
we feed him according to his own word,
it follows that the first clause is where he says: I need (to eat)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the answer in Step 9 and attacks it from the wording of the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 9, that the רישא is about a patient who says he does not need food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא is about a patient who says he needs food, so the רישא is probably the same patient. That means the experts override him, which goes against רבי ינאי.

steps.title: The משנה has missing words and should be read this way
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is missing words. The experts decide only when the patient says he does not need food. If he says he needs food and only one expert disagrees, we feed him based on his own word.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: When do we say the experts decide? When he says 'I do not need.' But if he says 'I need,' and instead of two experts there is only one who says he does not need, we feed him based on his own word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the משנה has missing words. It fills them in, so that the סיפא becomes a new case of a patient who says he needs food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words filled in, the רישא stays about a patient who says he does not need food, as Step 9 said. The סיפא is now a separate case: the patient says he needs food and only one expert disagrees. In that case the patient's own word wins, which fits רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: (The משנה) is missing words
And this is what it teaches
In what case was this said?
I need (to eat)

steps.whatToRemember: The רישא is about a patient who says he does not need food, so the experts decide. The סיפא is about a patient who says he needs food: if only one expert disagrees, we follow the patient.
steps.confusionAlert: In the reading with the missing words filled in, 'אין שם בקיאין' does not mean there are no experts at all. It means there are not two experts disagreeing, only one.

phrases.english: The mishna is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
In what case is this said?
Where he says: I do not need,
but if he said: I need,
and there are not two experts there
but only one who says: he does not need,
we feed him according to his own word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by reading the משנה with missing words, which keeps Step 9's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא suggested the רישא is about a patient who says he needs food, so the experts would override him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about a patient who says he does not need food. The סיפא is a new case: he says he needs food and only one expert disagrees, so we follow him.

steps.title: The patient's own word beats even a hundred experts
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי rules that whenever the patient says he needs food, we listen to him even if a hundred experts disagree, because 'the heart knows the bitterness of its soul.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: Any time the sick person says 'I need to eat,' even if there are a hundred experts who say he does not need to, we listen to him. The פסוק says: 'The heart knows the bitterness of its soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי gives a stronger view than Step 17. In his view, the patient's 'I need' wins against any number of experts, not only against one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 only said the patient beats one expert. מר בר רב אשי says the number of experts makes no difference at all. His reason is a פסוק: a person feels his own inner suffering better than anyone outside can measure it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I need' (to eat)
We listen to him (the patient himself)
'The heart knows the bitterness of its soul' (משלי 14:10)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the practical rule: a sick person who says he must eat on יום כפור is fed, no matter how many experts disagree.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Any case where he says 'I need' to eat,
even if there are a hundred
who say he does not need to,
we listen to him himself,
as it is said: 'The heart knows the bitterness of its soul.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר צָרִיךְ אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens Step 17's answer: the patient beats any number of experts, not only one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the patient says he needs food, we feed him even against a hundred experts.

steps.title: The משנה seems to say experts matter when present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges מר בר רב אשי. The משנה says we follow the patient 'if there are no experts,' which implies that when experts are present, we do not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If there are no experts there, we feed him based on his own word. So the reason is only because there are no experts. But if there are experts, we would not feed him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks מר בר רב אשי using a precise reading of the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'if there are no experts' suggests the opposite case: when experts are present, they decide even against the patient. That clashes with מר בר רב אשי, who says the patient's 'I need' always wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on his own word
'The reason is because... but otherwise': a style of drawing an inference from the opposite case

phrases.english: We learned:
If there are no experts there,
we feed him based on his own word.
The reason is that there are no experts;
but if there are experts, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 18 from the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's rule that the patient beats any number of experts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the patient's word depend on no experts being present, so experts who are present should override him.

steps.title: When the patient says 'I need,' it is as if no experts are there at all
steps.stepSummary: The משנה should be read this way: experts decide only when the patient says 'I do not need.' When he says 'I need,' the experts count as if they were not there at all, and we feed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: When is it true that we follow the experts? When the patient says 'I do not need.' But if he says 'I need,' it is as if there are no experts there at all, and we feed him based on his own word. The פסוק says: 'The heart knows the bitterness of its soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends מר בר רב אשי by re-reading the משנה. The words 'no experts' are understood as 'the experts do not count.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'no experts' does not mean experts are physically missing. It means that once the patient says 'I need,' their opinion is ignored completely. So the משנה fully matches מר בר רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means': a re-reading of a text
'When is this said?': limiting a rule to a certain case
At all

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: if the patient says 'I need to eat,' we feed him on יום כפור no matter how many experts disagree. Experts decide only when he says he does not need to eat.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין שם בקיאין כלל' does not mean the experts left the room. It means their opinion is treated as if it did not exist.

phrases.english: This is what it means:
When is this said?
When he said 'I do not need.'
But if he said 'I need,'
there are no experts there at all;
we feed him based on his own word,
as it is said: 'The heart knows the bitterness of its soul.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by re-reading the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No experts' means experts are physically absent, so experts who are present would override the patient.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No experts at all' means that once the patient says 'I need,' the experts' opinion is treated as nothing.

steps.title: New משנה: בולמוס and the mad dog bite
steps.stepSummary: A person seized by בולמוס may be fed even impure foods until his eyes brighten. A person bitten by a mad dog may not be fed the dog's liver lobe, but רבי מתיא בן חרש permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone seized by בולמוס (a dangerous, overwhelming hunger) may be fed even impure foods until his eyes light up again. Someone bitten by a mad dog may not be fed the lobe of that dog's liver. רבי מתיא בן חרש permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses which forbidden things we may give to a person in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With בולמוס, the danger is real, so even forbidden food is allowed until the eyes brighten, which shows he is recovering. With the mad dog, the dispute is whether the liver remedy actually works. The חכמים say it does not, so the prohibition stays. רבי מתיא בן חרש holds that it works, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
A dangerous illness of extreme hunger that also weakens the eyesight
Impure (forbidden) foods
Until his eyes light up (a sign of recovery)
A mad (rabid) dog
The lobe of the liver

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים do not forbid the liver because saving a life is unimportant. They forbid it because they hold that this remedy does not work.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who is seized by bulmos,
we feed him even impure foods,
until his eyes light up.
One whom a mad dog bit,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲצַר כָּבֵד שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: we do not feed him from the lobe of its liver.
And Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the sick-person discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with בולמוס may be fed forbidden food until he recovers. A mad dog's liver is forbidden according to the חכמים and permitted according to רבי מתיא בן חרש.

steps.title: Medicine for throat pain on שבת because of ספק נפשות
steps.stepSummary: רבי מתיא בן חרש rules that we may put medicine in the mouth of someone with throat pain on שבת. Such pain may be life-threatening, and any doubt about danger to life overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מתיא בן חרש also said: Someone who has pain in his throat may have medicine put into his mouth on שבת. This is because it might be dangerous to his life, and any doubt about danger to life pushes aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second ruling from רבי מתיא בן חרש. Medicine for throat pain is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, giving medicine on שבת is forbidden. Pain inside the throat is hard to judge, so we cannot be sure whether it is dangerous. The משנה then states a general rule: even a doubt about danger to life overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has pain in his throat
Medicine
A doubt about danger to life
Overrides (pushes aside) שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Big rule: כל ספק נפשות דוחה את השבת. Even a doubt about danger to life overrides שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general principle leads into the famous discussion in the גמרא about the source for the rule that saving a life overrides שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ:
phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash said:
One who has pain in his throat,

phrases.aramaic: מְטִילִין לוֹ סַם בְּתוֹךְ פִּיו בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: we may put medicine inside his mouth on Shabbat,
because it is a possible danger to life,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל סְפֵק נְפָשׁוֹת דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and any possible danger to life overrides Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling from רבי מתיא בן חרש in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Medicine may be given for throat pain on שבת, because any doubt about danger to life overrides שבת.

steps.title: Digging out a person trapped under a collapse on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that we clear a collapsed pile on שבת even if we are unsure whether a person is under it, whether he is alive, or whether he is Jewish. If he is found alive we keep digging. If he is dead we leave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a pile collapsed on someone, and we don't know if he is there or not, alive or dead, a non-Jew or a Jew, we clear the pile off him. If they found him alive, they keep clearing. If he is dead, they leave him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case of saving a life on שבת: a person who may be buried under fallen debris.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stacks three separate doubts: is he there, is he alive, is he Jewish. Even with all of them, we still break שבת to dig. Once we know he is dead, there is no life left to save, so we stop.

keyTerms.meaning: A collapse; falling debris or a fallen building
Doubt; an uncertain situation
We clear away the pile of debris
They should leave him (do not keep digging)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source that even a doubtful chance of saving a life (ספק פיקוח נפש) overrides שבת.

phrases.english: One upon whom a collapse fell,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק הוּא שָׁם סָפֵק אֵינוֹ שָׁם,
phrases.english: it is uncertain whether he is there or not there,
uncertain whether alive or dead,
uncertain whether a gentile or a Jew,
we clear the pile off him.
If they found him alive, they keep clearing,
and if he is dead, they leave him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of life-saving cases that override שבת, after the cases of the sick person and the person with בולמוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We clear debris on שבת even when there is a triple doubt. We continue if he is alive and stop if he is dead.

steps.title: How do we know the starving person has recovered?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how we can tell that the eyes of a person with בולמוס have 'brightened,' meaning he has recovered enough to stop being fed forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא. Our Rabbis taught: How would they know that his eyes had brightened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the בולמוס line of the משנה and quotes a ברייתא asking what the sign of recovery is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said we feed him 'until his eyes brighten.' That is the point where the permission to feed him forbidden food ends, so we need a clear test for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא section that discusses the משנה
His eyes brightened (he has recovered)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא here is not yet discussing the מפולת case you just read. It jumps back to the earlier בולמוס case in the משנה.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Our Rabbis taught:
From where would they know that his eyes had brightened?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the בולמוס ruling from step 21 to define its endpoint.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the sign that the person with בולמוס has recovered?

steps.title: The sign is telling good food from bad
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that he has recovered once he can tell the difference between good and bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when he can tell the difference between good and bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question by giving the sign of recovery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person with בולמוס eats anything without noticing what it is. Once he can tell good food from bad food again, his senses have come back and he is out of danger.

keyTerms.meaning: He will distinguish or tell apart
Between good and bad

phrases.english: From when he can distinguish between good and bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He has recovered once he can tell good from bad.

steps.title: אביי explains that the test is done by taste
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'telling good from bad' means telling flavors apart by tasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And by taste.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains how the ברייתא's test is done: by taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said he recovers when he can tell good from bad. אביי specifies that this is judged by taste: once he can tell flavors apart, his senses, and his eyesight with them, have returned. According to the מאירי, this test works even at night, when he cannot see.

keyTerms.meaning: By taste

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And by taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to or refines the ברייתא's answer in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's test of telling good from bad is done by tasting.

steps.title: Feed the starving person the lightest prohibition first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a person with בולמוס is fed the least severe forbidden food first. Between טבל and נבילה, we feed him נבילה. Between טבל and שביעית, we feed him שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: One seized by בולמוס is fed the lighter prohibition first. If there is טבל and נבילה, we feed him נבילה. If there is טבל and שביעית, we feed him שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא teaching which forbidden food comes first when we must feed someone with בולמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when breaking a prohibition is allowed to save a life, we choose the smallest one. טבל carries death at the hands of Heaven, while נבילה is only a לאו with lashes. שביעית has no punishment at all, so both are lighter than טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The lightest first, step by step
Produce not yet tithed (eating it carries death at the hands of Heaven)
Meat of an animal not properly slaughtered
Produce of the Sabbatical year

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle: when a prohibition must be broken, choose the least severe one.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
One who is seized by bulmos,
we feed him the lightest first.
Untithed produce and a carcass: we feed him the carcass.
Untithed produce and Sabbatical produce: the Sabbatical produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בולמוס topic, moving from when to stop feeding him to what order to feed him in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feed the least severe prohibition first: נבילה before טבל, and שביעית before טבל.

steps.title: טבל versus תרומה is a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the choice between טבל and תרומה is a disagreement among תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Untithed produce and תרומה: it is a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a harder pair and says the תנאים disagree about it. This sets up the source quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier pairs, there is no clear answer here. Both טבל and תרומה carry death at the hands of Heaven for a non-כהן, so it is not obvious which is lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים
It is a dispute among תנאים

phrases.english: Untithed produce and terumah: it is a dispute of tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a pair of foods that step 27 did not cover.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Which to feed first, טבל or תרומה, is disputed.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the dispute: the תנא קמא says feed him טבל and not תרומה, while בן תימא says feed him תרומה and not טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: We feed him טבל and do not feed him תרומה. בן תימא says: תרומה and not טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that proves this is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא feeds טבל, so he must hold that תרומה is the more severe prohibition. בן תימא feeds תרומה, so he must hold that טבל is more severe. The גמרא gives the actual reasoning of each side in Steps 32 and 33.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
We feed him untithed produce
and we do not feed him terumah.
Ben Teima says:
Terumah and not untithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That טבל versus תרומה is a dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the תנא קמא and בן תימא

steps.title: רבה: if the produce can be tithed, tithe it and feed him
steps.stepSummary: רבה limits the dispute. When it is possible to make the טבל into permitted חולין by tithing it, everyone agrees that we tithe it and feed it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Where it is possible to give him חולין, everyone agrees that we fix it for him and feed it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה narrows the argument from the previous step. It applies only when the טבל cannot be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we can separate the tithes and make the food fully permitted, then no one would choose a forbidden food. The תנאים argue only when tithing is not possible. Separating tithes on שבת is normally forbidden, but here it is allowed because it avoids a more severe prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy, permitted food
We fix it (by separating the tithes)
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: With a person seized by בולמוס, we feed him the lightest prohibition first. If we can turn טבל into permitted food by tithing it, everyone agrees we do that and then feed him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that if a forbidden act can be avoided entirely, we must avoid it, even when saving a life.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
Where it is possible with non-sacred food,
everyone agrees
that we fix it for him and feed it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר בְּחוּלִּין, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the dispute of step 29 to cases where the טבל cannot be tithed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the טבל can be tithed, everyone agrees we tithe it and feed him permitted food.

steps.title: The dispute is only when the food cannot be made into חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבה continues: the תנאים argue only in a case where the טבל cannot be tithed and turned into permitted חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When do they argue? In a case where it is not possible to turn the food into permitted חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is finishing his point from the last step. Now he tells us exactly which case the תנא קמא and בן תימא are arguing about. This sets up the explanation of their reasoning in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 30, רבה said that if the טבל can be tithed, everyone agrees to tithe it, even on שבת. So the argument must be about a case where there is no way to tithe it and make it permitted. In that case we must feed him a forbidden food, and the question is which one.

keyTerms.meaning: When they argue / where they disagree
Possible
Ordinary, non-sacred food that is permitted to eat

phrases.english: When they disagree
phrases.notes: "They" are the תנא קמא and בן תימא from Step 29.

phrases.english: it is where it is not possible to make it into non-sacred food.
phrases.notes: That is, where there is no way to separate the tithes and make the טבל permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's limitation of the dispute by naming the case where the disagreement actually applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between the תנא קמא and בן תימא applies only when the טבל cannot be made into permitted חולין.

steps.title: Each side holds a different prohibition is more severe
steps.stepSummary: One opinion holds that טבל is more severe, and the other holds that תרומה is more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that טבל is more severe, and one Sage holds that תרומה is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us the root of the argument. The two תנאים disagree about which forbidden food carries the heavier prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 set the rule that we feed the person the least severe forbidden food first. So whoever thinks טבל is more severe will feed תרומה, and whoever thinks תרומה is more severe will feed טבל. This matches the two views in Step 29: בן תימא feeds תרומה because he holds טבל is more severe, and the תנא קמא feeds טבל because he holds תרומה is more severe.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage holds
More severe, a heavier prohibition
Produce from which תרומות ומעשרות have not yet been separated
The portion given to a כהן, which is forbidden to a non-כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' is not the תנא קמא. The one who holds טבל is more severe is בן תימא, who feeds תרומה. The one who holds תרומה is more severe is the תנא קמא, who feeds טבל.

phrases.english: One Sage holds that untithed produce is more severe,
phrases.notes: This is בן תימא, so he feeds תרומה.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds that teruma is more severe.
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, so he feeds טבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר טֶבֶל חָמוּר, וּמַר סָבַר תְּרוּמָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case has been defined, the גמרא names the underlying point of disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute depends on whether טבל or תרומה is the more severe prohibition.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: The טבל-is-more-severe side argues that תרומה is permitted to a כהן. The תרומה-is-more-severe side argues that טבל can be fixed by tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who holds טבל is more severe reasons that תרומה is at least fit for a כהן. The one who holds תרומה is more severe reasons that טבל can be fixed by tithing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each opinion and adds its reason. It explains why each side sees the other food as the lighter prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first side, טבל is forbidden to everyone, while תרומה is permitted to a כהן, so תרומה is a lighter prohibition. For the second side, תרומה can never become permitted to a non-כהן, while טבל can become permitted once it is tithed, so טבל is a lighter prohibition. The two sides use different measures: who is allowed to eat the food, versus whether the food can be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is fit, may be used
A priest, who is allowed to eat תרומה
To fix it, meaning to make it permitted by separating the tithes

steps.whatToRemember: When food cannot be tithed, בן תימא feeds תרומה because טבל is forbidden to everyone. The תנא קמא feeds טבל because it can be fixed, while תרומה can never become permitted to a non-כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two different ways to measure how severe a prohibition is: by how many people it forbids, or by whether the forbidden status can ever be removed.

phrases.english: One Sage holds that untithed produce is more severe,
phrases.notes: Because it is forbidden to everyone, even a כהן.

phrases.english: but teruma is fit for a priest.
phrases.notes: So תרומה is the lighter prohibition.

phrases.english: And one Sage holds that teruma is more severe,
phrases.notes: Because a non-כהן can never eat it.

phrases.english: but untithed produce can be fixed.
phrases.notes: Tithing makes it permitted, so its prohibition is lighter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר טֶבֶל חָמוּר — אֲבָל תְּרוּמָה חַזְיָא לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the two positions from Step 32 in order to add the reason behind each one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טבל is more severe because תרומה is permitted to a כהן. תרומה is more severe because טבל can be fixed by tithing.
